title: Proactive capacity fencepost: mitigate surge-induced reserved pool undershoot
creator: Ethan Miller
description: Summary: Several customers experienced brief but repeated capacity shortfalls during tightly spaced traffic surges. Investigation shows a timing mismatch between the autoscaler's horizon math and the reserved-pool commit window (a fencepost/rounding edge case). The platform transiently undershoots reserved capacity for affected tenants for ~10-30s during back-to-back microbursts, triggering customer escalations and elevated p99 latency. This ticket tracks the bugfix, short-term mitigations, rollout plan, and post-incident safeguards.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a reserved pool with warmup credit enabled and tenant priority weighting > 1.0
Using the load-test harness (tools/perf/burst-simulator), emit two 30s microbursts separated by a 20s lull tuned to autoscaler horizon (H=45s) and warmup_delay (D=15s).
Observe reserved-pool headroom dip below desired_target and subsequent request queuing or on-demand fallback for high-priority tenants.
Reproduce also with heterogeneous GPU backends (A100 + T4) to surface kernel selection slow-start effects that exacerbate rounding mismatches.
root_cause: The autoscaler computes target reservation using a discrete horizon window and then floors the reservation when converting to slot counts. Meanwhile reserved-pool commit cycles use a separate inclusive window. For rapid repeated surges the combined effect produces a 1-slot fencepost undercommit for small-tenants and leads to immediate queuing or preemptions. Telemetry propagation lag (~2-6s) and warmup credit accounting rounding amplify the undershoot into customer-visible throttling.
impact: Affects small-to-medium tenants with burst budgets and strict low-latency SLAs. Customers reported transient 5-15x p99 latency increases and several escalations from payment and healthcare tenants. No data loss; the customer-facing effect is increased latency and failed requests when on-demand fallback is not configured.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Apply immediate autoscaler patch to add a +1 slot safety margin for any reservation calculation that results from discrete horizon arithmetic. 2) Increase default short-window headroom multiplier to 1.15 for P0/P1 tenants. 3) Enable aggressive on-demand fallback for affected tenants while patch rolls out. 4) Notify affected customers with mitigation steps and temporary credits.
proposed_fix: Rewrite reservation math to use inclusive interval semantics and switch to ceiling() when converting fractional reservations to slot counts. Add a deterministic reconciliation job that runs every 10s to detect and heal 1-slot undercommits. Extend metrics emission to include reservation_delta and commit_latency so we can alert at 1-slot divergence.
implementation_notes:
- Primary change in autoscaler/reservation_calculator.go. Add tests for edge patterns (alternating microburst sequences).
- Add e2e perf test in tools/perf that reproduces the 2-burst pattern.
- Reconcile warmup credit ledger rounding to use consistent fixed-point arithmetic to avoid drift across components.
- Ensure change is tolerant on heterogeneous GPU pools (explicit slot mapping table).
rollout_plan: 1) Land change behind feature flag 'fencepost_safe_reservations'. 2) Canary 10% of reserved-pool controllers in us-west-2 for 2 hours with synthetic microburst job running. 3) If canary green (no 1-slot deltas for 30m), increase to 50% and run for 4 hours. 4) Full rollout across regions in staged waves (EU then APAC). 5) Post-rollout, enable reconciliation job globally and disable the feature flag after 72h of clean telemetry.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: reserved_pool.reservation_delta (slots) — alert if > 0 for > 30s
Existing: tenant.p99_latency — increase alert sensitivity during rollout (thresholds -20%)
Dashboards: add 'fencepost guard' panel with per-tenant 1-slot events and warmup-credit drift
rollback_strategy: If canary shows increased errors or customer impact: rollback autoscaler and enable emergency +2 slot safety margin in the controller, revert feature flag to off, and execute cross-region failover to cold-pool capacity for affected tenants.
customer_communications: Sent targeted outbound email to tenants flagged by headroom_anomaly pipeline explaining transient risk and applying 10% credits
Posted incident notice to status.redwood.com with timeline and ETA for fix
Scheduled follow-up calls with top-affected customers (OrbitPay, AcmeHealth equivalents) to review mitigation and SLAs
progress_updates: 2025-02-16: Initial triage — reproduced locally with burst-simulator. Identified fencepost mismatch hypothesis.
2025-02-18: Hotpatch deployed to add temporary +1 slot margin for affected tenants; observed reduction in customer alerts.
2025-02-22: Implemented fixed-point warmup credit accounting prototype; unit tests added.
2025-02-28: RFC for inclusive-interval reservation arithmetic reviewed by runtime and infra — approved with minor comments.
2025-03-03: Feature flagged change landed behind 'fencepost_safe_reservations'; canary started in us-west-2.
postmortem_actions: Add determinism tests for horizon-edge patterns into CI (tools/perf/test-cases/edge-horizon)
Instrument autoscaler with reservation_delta metric and surface in Console alerts
Run quarterly chaos tests that simulate repeated microbursts with heterogeneous GPUs
Document recommended tenant config defaults for bursty workloads in the public docs
